6	# Contributing
7	
8	This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
9	FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
10	firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
11	rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
12	alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
13	owner** before you open it.
14	
15	## Roles
16	
17	Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
18	the people who write ours.
19	
20	- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
21	  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
22	  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
23	  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
24	  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
25	- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
26	  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
27	  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
28	  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
29	  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.
30	
31	Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
32	and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
33	sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
34	EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.
35	
36	## Clean-room rules
37	
38	### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes
39	
40	- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
41	  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
42	- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
43	- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
44	  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
45	- any other FM-1 firmware source;
46	- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
47	  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
48	- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
49	  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
50	  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
51	  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
52	  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
53	  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
54	  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
55	  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
56	  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
57	  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
58	- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.
59	
60	`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
61	this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).
62	
63	### Firmware side may use
64	
65	Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
66	was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:
67	
68	- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
69	  source);
70	- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
71	  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
72	- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
73	  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
74	  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
75	- public datasheets;
76	- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
77	  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
78	- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
79	  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.
80	
81	### Barriers
82	
83	- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
84	  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
85	  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
86	  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
87	  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
88	  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
89	  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
90	  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
91	  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
92	  `config/claude/spec.json`.
93	- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
94	  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
95	- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
96	  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
97	  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
98	  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
99	  non-zero if they differ.
100	- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
101	  of every session, before anything else:
102	  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
103	     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
104	     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
105	     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
106	     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
107	     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
108	  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
109	  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
110	  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.
111	
112	### Spec-side text discipline
113	
114	What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
115	and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
116	sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
117	the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
118	titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
119	`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
120	changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
121	addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
122	comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
123	results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
124	`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
125	occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
126	by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
127	on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors.
128	
129	## Commit messages
130	
131	Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
132	it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):
133	
134	```
135	<area>: <what changed, one line>
136	
137	What:    what this commit does
138	Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
139	How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
140	Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
141	Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
142	Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
143	```
144	
145	- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
146	  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
147	- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
148	- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
149	  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
150	  the agent; the owner is the committer.
151	- Small commits: one idea each.
152	- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
153	  carries the sections.
154	
155	`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).
156	
157	## Pull requests and merging
158	
159	- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
160	  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
161	  links to the CI run and the record).
162	- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
163	- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
164	  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
165	  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
166	  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
167	- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
168	  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main.
169	- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
170	  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
171	  SBOM.
172	
173	### Merge policy and its history
174	
175	- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
176	  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
177	  with GitHub's key instead.
178	- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
179	  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
180	  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
181	  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
182	- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
183	  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.
184	
185	What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
186	by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
187	button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
188	The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
189	(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
190	the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
191	as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
192	run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
193	is still written.
194	
195	## Rulesets
196	
197	Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):
198	
199	- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
200	  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
201	  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
202	  role).
203	- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
204	  pushes; no bypass.
205	- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
206	  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
207	  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
208	- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
209	  bypass.
210	
211	Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
212	off).
213	
214	Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
215	GitHub API:
216	
217	| What | ID or fingerprint |
218	|------|-------------------|
219	| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
220	| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
221	| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
222	| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
223	| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
224	| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |
225	
226	The deploy key's private half was generated in the session's scratch
227	folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
228	deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
229	public key, delete the old key.
230	
231	## SSH signing for milestone tags (one-time setup, owner)
232	
233	1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):
234	   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
235	2. Tell git to sign with it:
236	   ```sh
237	   git config --global gpg.format ssh
238	   git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub
239	   git config --global tag.gpgSign true
240	   ```
241	   Leave `commit.gpgSign` off: merges are signed by GitHub's button.
242	3. Let git verify signatures locally: add a line
243	   `<your git email> <contents of id_ed25519_signing.pub>` to
244	   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
245	   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
246	4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
247	   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
248	5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
249	6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
250	   tag as **Verified**.
251	
252	## Licences
253	
254	- Every file we write starts with an SPDX header:
255	  `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and `SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98`.
256	  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
257	- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
258	- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
259	- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
260	- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
261	  repository is public and history is never rewritten.
262	
263	## Low profile (for now)
264	
265	The repository is public but unpromoted. In its name, description and topics,
266	and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
267	firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
268	patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
269	announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
270	docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

# M0c review of docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md

## Summary

I read only `docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, using the rules in sections 1 and 2 of the M0c prompt. The spec has 47 entries (HW-1 to HW-47) and 12 open questions (Q-1 to Q-12).

The document is well structured. I found no code, pseudo-code or init sequence copied from source, and nothing that is plainly taken from forbidden material. It is not ready to release yet:

- **One wrong command code:** HW-31 gives `0x22` as inversion off.
